newsitem.title: USA: US Sen Chafee opposes delay of ISTEA bill debate.
newsitem.headline: US Sen Chafee opposes delay of ISTEA bill debate.

text.p: U.S. Sen. John Chafee said Friday he opposes efforts by some senators to delay until next year enactment of a multi-year surface transportation funding law.

The Rhode Island Republican, who chairs the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, warned that a growing collection of funding proposals and mounting "disputes" over fiscal 1998 transportation spending have led some members of Congress to push for a one-year time-out on the debate.

The strategy, Chafee said in a press statement, is to reauthorize the Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act of 1991 for one year and then resume debate on a broader reauthorization bill in 1998.
But Chafee said a one-year bill would unnecessarily tie up valuable Senate floor time and weaken Congress' abililty to set a strong national transportation policy.
"The significant uncertainly that would result from a one-year extension would paralyze the states and lead to a continued deterioration of today's transportation network," Chafee said.
Chafee said his panel is drafting a bill to reauthorize ISTEA for six years and hopes to take "further action" on the proposals following Congress' one-week July 4 recess.
